w-full flex-col gap-1 empty:hidden first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full break-words dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="444">Short answer: <strong data-start="14" data-end="140">yes — attackers can and do try to repurpose compromised cloud hosts (including GPU-equipped VMs) to run heavy ML workloads</strong>,
 but doing so leaves a collection of measurable signals. Below I give a 
defensible, non-actionable detection and response playbook (for SOCs, 
CISOs, cloud ops, and incident responders) that you can implement 
immediately to spot GPU abuse, prevent large-scale covert training, and 
respond if you find it.</p>
<p data-start="446" data-end="457">I’ll cover:</p>
<ol data-start="458" data-end="724">
<li data-start="458" data-end="524">
<p data-start="461" data-end="524">high-level threat model (what “GPU botnet” abuse looks like),</p>
</li>
<li data-start="525" data-end="589">
<p data-start="528" data-end="589">the strongest detectors (cloud + host + network telemetry),</p>
</li>
<li data-start="590" data-end="646">
<p data-start="593" data-end="646">practical SIEM/hunt ideas and artifacts to collect,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="647" data-end="687">
<p data-start="650" data-end="687">response &amp; forensics checklist, and</p>
</li>
<li data-start="688" data-end="724">
<p data-start="691" data-end="724">prioritized quick wins for CISOs.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="726" data-end="729">
<h2 data-start="731" data-end="799">1) Threat model — what “GPU abuse” looks like (defensive framing)</h2>
<p data-start="800" data-end="878">Attackers who want GPU capacity typically try one or more of these approaches:</p>
<ul data-start="880" data-end="1425">
<li data-start="880" data-end="1015">
<p data-start="882" data-end="1015"><strong data-start="882" data-end="911">Repurpose compromised VMs</strong> (infected Linux servers, compromised cloud credentials) to run ML training jobs (PyTorch/TensorFlow).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1016" data-end="1126">
<p data-start="1018" data-end="1126"><strong data-start="1018" data-end="1051">Rent or steal cloud instances</strong> using stolen/instrumented cloud creds, then run training or fine-tuning.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1127" data-end="1213">
<p data-start="1129" data-end="1213"><strong data-start="1129" data-end="1160">Lease GPU-for-hire services</strong> on underground markets (less stealthy but common).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1214" data-end="1309">
<p data-start="1216" data-end="1309"><strong data-start="1216" data-end="1256">Hijack container/kubernetes clusters</strong> that expose GPUs (schedule pods using GPU taints).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1310" data-end="1425">
<p data-start="1312" data-end="1425"><strong data-start="1312" data-end="1345">Use botnets of commodity GPUs</strong> in hijacked workstations/servers where attackers launch distributed training.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1427" data-end="1585">They <strong data-start="1432" data-end="1466">don’t need to be sophisticated</strong> to cause damage — even short bursts of heavy GPU use let them train/finetune smaller models or run inference at scale.</p>
<p data-start="1587" data-end="1744"><strong data-start="1587" data-end="1616">Important defensive note:</strong> I will <em data-start="1624" data-end="1629">not</em> provide instructions on how to do any of the above. The rest of this message focuses on detection and remediation.</p>
<hr data-start="1746" data-end="1749">
<h2 data-start="1751" data-end="1834">2) Best detectors — where to look (cloud + host + network + financial telemetry)</h2>
<h3 data-start="1836" data-end="1890">Cloud provider / billing telemetry (highest value)</h3>
<ul data-start="1891" data-end="2452">
<li data-start="1891" data-end="2028">
<p data-start="1893" data-end="2028"><strong data-start="1893" data-end="1939">Billing spikes / new Niched instance types</strong> — sudden increases in spending on GPU instance families (A100/H100/GV100/MI300, etc.).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2029" data-end="2149">
<p data-start="2031" data-end="2149"><strong data-start="2031" data-end="2067">New or unusual instance creation</strong> — alerts on creation of <code data-start="2092" data-end="2097">gpu</code> instances from unusual accounts, IPs, or regions.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2150" data-end="2272">
<p data-start="2152" data-end="2272"><strong data-start="2152" data-end="2182">Short-lived credential use</strong> — many ephemeral API tokens, service keys, or IAM role creations in short time windows.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2273" data-end="2368">
<p data-start="2275" data-end="2368"><strong data-start="2275" data-end="2307">Unusual SSH/console activity</strong> for accounts that don’t normally use interactive sessions.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2369" data-end="2452">
<p data-start="2371" data-end="2452"><strong data-start="2371" data-end="2425">Cloud audit logs showing GPU resource provisioning</strong> — correlate with identity.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2454" data-end="2598">Why monitor this first: providers 
produce logs and billing data you can alert on centrally — this is the 
fastest way to detect large GPU misuse.</p>
<hr data-start="2600" data-end="2603">
<h3 data-start="2605" data-end="2651">Host / container telemetry (next priority)</h3>
<ul data-start="2652" data-end="3697">
<li data-start="2652" data-end="2789">
<p data-start="2654" data-end="2789"><strong data-start="2654" data-end="2688">Sustained high GPU utilization</strong> on hosts that normally don’t run ML (GPU % utilization, GPU memory used, power draw, temperature).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2790" data-end="2957">
<p data-start="2792" data-end="2957"><strong data-start="2792" data-end="2838">Long-running python or container processes</strong> invoking ML frameworks (<code data-start="2863" data-end="2880">python -m torch</code>, <code data-start="2882" data-end="2908">python -c "import torch"</code>, long <code data-start="2915" data-end="2923">python</code> processes with high GPU usage).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2958" data-end="3139">
<p data-start="2960" data-end="3139"><strong data-start="2960" data-end="2988">Presence of ML artifacts</strong>: model files (<code data-start="3003" data-end="3009">*.pt</code>, <code data-start="3011" data-end="3018">*.bin</code>, <code data-start="3020" data-end="3028">*.ckpt</code>), optimizer/state files, dataset shards (<code data-start="3070" data-end="3076">.tar</code>, <code data-start="3078" data-end="3084">.npz</code>), training logs (TensorBoard, <code data-start="3115" data-end="3135">trainer_state.json</code>).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3140" data-end="3293">
<p data-start="3142" data-end="3293"><strong data-start="3142" data-end="3171">Known ML container images</strong> running where they shouldn’t (images named <code data-start="3215" data-end="3224">pytorch</code>, <code data-start="3226" data-end="3238">tensorflow</code>, <code data-start="3240" data-end="3266">huggingface/transformers</code>, <code data-start="3268" data-end="3283">deep-learning</code>, etc.).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3294" data-end="3443">
<p data-start="3296" data-end="3443"><strong data-start="3296" data-end="3322">New packages installed</strong>: <code data-start="3324" data-end="3331">torch</code>, <code data-start="3333" data-end="3345">tensorflow</code>, <code data-start="3347" data-end="3361">transformers</code>, <code data-start="3363" data-end="3375">accelerate</code>, <code data-start="3377" data-end="3391">bitsandbytes</code>, CUDA toolchains in environments not used for ML.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3444" data-end="3585">
<p data-start="3446" data-end="3585"><strong data-start="3446" data-end="3495">GPU device environment variables / visibility</strong> used in containers (<code data-start="3516" data-end="3538">CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES</code>, <code data-start="3540" data-end="3564">NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES</code>) unexpectedly set.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3586" data-end="3697">
<p data-start="3588" data-end="3697"><strong data-start="3588" data-end="3625">Unusual use of orchestration APIs</strong> (Kubernetes API creating pods that request <code data-start="3669" data-end="3685">nvidia.com/gpu</code> resources).</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3699" data-end="3773">These are strong host-level indicators and often yield forensic artifacts.</p>
<hr data-start="3775" data-end="3778">
<h3 data-start="3780" data-end="3811">Network &amp; storage telemetry</h3>
<ul data-start="3812" data-end="4447">
<li data-start="3812" data-end="3995">
<p data-start="3814" data-end="3995"><strong data-start="3814" data-end="3840">Large outbound uploads</strong>
 to S3/Blob storage, multi-gigabyte uploads over short windows — often 
the attacker exfiltrates datasets or writes model checkpoints to 
external buckets.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3996" data-end="4137">
<p data-start="3998" data-end="4137"><strong data-start="3998" data-end="4036">Connections to known dataset hosts</strong> or to huggingface.co, private storage endpoints, or unusual domain names related to model sharing.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4138" data-end="4234">
<p data-start="4140" data-end="4234"><strong data-start="4140" data-end="4174">High egress from compute nodes</strong> to unfamiliar IPs (look for patterns of chunked uploads).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4235" data-end="4334">
<p data-start="4237" data-end="4334"><strong data-start="4237" data-end="4267">Use of storage signed URLs</strong> or public buckets created shortly before/after GPU provisioning.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4335" data-end="4447">
<p data-start="4337" data-end="4447"><strong data-start="4337" data-end="4377">C2 traffic + pulled container images</strong> — exfiltration or fetching of runner images from external registries.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="4449" data-end="4452">
<h3 data-start="4454" data-end="4528">Financial/blockchain telemetry (if extortion / monetization suspected)</h3>
<ul data-start="4529" data-end="4680">
<li data-start="4529" data-end="4588">
<p data-start="4531" data-end="4588"><strong data-start="4531" data-end="4557">Wallets/exchange flows</strong> tied to ransomware/BEC IOCs.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4589" data-end="4680">
<p data-start="4591" data-end="4680"><strong data-start="4591" data-end="4623">Payments that precede spikes</strong> in cloud spend (useful for law enforcement correlation).</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="4682" data-end="4685">
<h2 data-start="4687" data-end="4772">3) Practical hunt queries &amp; artifacts to search for (SOC-friendly, non-actionable)</h2>
<p data-start="4774" data-end="4906">Below are <em data-start="4784" data-end="4796">conceptual</em> SIEM hunts and artifact types — you can translate to Splunk/Elastic/CarbonBlack queries for your environment.</p>
<ul data-start="4908" data-end="6198">
<li data-start="4908" data-end="5080">
<p data-start="4910" data-end="5080"><strong data-start="4910" data-end="4925">Cloud audit</strong>: search CloudTrail / Cloud Audit logs for <code data-start="4968" data-end="4982">RunInstances</code> or <code data-start="4986" data-end="5002">CreateInstance</code> where <code data-start="5009" data-end="5023">instanceType</code> ∈ GPU families AND <code data-start="5043" data-end="5054">principal</code> not in known dev lists.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5081" data-end="5183">
<p data-start="5083" data-end="5183"><strong data-start="5083" data-end="5102">Billing anomaly</strong>: alert if <code data-start="5113" data-end="5131">weekly GPU spend</code> &gt; baseline * X (X = 3–5) or if <code data-start="5163" data-end="5174">GPU hours</code> spike.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5184" data-end="5341">
<p data-start="5186" data-end="5341"><strong data-start="5186" data-end="5218">Container image whitelisting</strong>: alert when an image with substring <code data-start="5255" data-end="5300">pytorch|tensorflow|transformers|huggingface</code> runs in a namespace not tagged for ML.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5342" data-end="5539">
<p data-start="5344" data-end="5539"><strong data-start="5344" data-end="5363">Process hunting</strong>: look for long-running <code data-start="5387" data-end="5395">python</code> processes with unusual cmdline length or with network activity &gt; N MB; flag if <code data-start="5475" data-end="5483">python</code> spawns <code data-start="5491" data-end="5504">tensorboard</code>, <code data-start="5506" data-end="5532">torch.distributed.launch</code> etc.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5540" data-end="5690">
<p data-start="5542" data-end="5690"><strong data-start="5542" data-end="5566">File artifact search</strong>: search for files with extensions <code data-start="5601" data-end="5606">.pt</code>, <code data-start="5608" data-end="5614">.bin</code>, <code data-start="5616" data-end="5623">.ckpt</code>, or folders named <code data-start="5642" data-end="5655">checkpoints</code>, <code data-start="5657" data-end="5671">checkpoints/</code> on non-ML hosts.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5691" data-end="5921">
<p data-start="5693" data-end="5921"><strong data-start="5693" data-end="5710">GPU telemetry</strong>: collect metrics from Cloud Monitoring or node exporters: <code data-start="5769" data-end="5786">gpu_utilization</code>, <code data-start="5788" data-end="5805">gpu_memory_used</code>, <code data-start="5807" data-end="5824">gpu_temperature</code>. Create alerts for sustained high values (e.g., &gt;70% for &gt;30 minutes) on assets not marked ML.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5922" data-end="6060">
<p data-start="5924" data-end="6060"><strong data-start="5924" data-end="5938">IMDS abuse</strong>: detect unusual reads to instance metadata (IMDS) combined with instance reconfigurations — common in credential theft.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6061" data-end="6198">
<p data-start="6063" data-end="6198"><strong data-start="6063" data-end="6085">S3 access patterns</strong>: flag large PutObject requests (&gt;1GB) within short intervals from compute nodes not associated with backup jobs.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="6200" data-end="6203">
<h2 data-start="6205" data-end="6279">4) Forensic &amp; evidence artifacts to collect (if you suspect compromise)</h2>
<p data-start="6280" data-end="6342">When you have a suspected machine, preserve artifacts quickly:</p>
<ul data-start="6344" data-end="7264">
<li data-start="6344" data-end="6465">
<p data-start="6346" data-end="6465"><strong data-start="6346" data-end="6381">Cloud provider logs &amp; snapshots</strong>: instance creation events, IAM actions, API calls, billing records, console logs.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6466" data-end="6565">
<p data-start="6468" data-end="6565"><strong data-start="6468" data-end="6487">Memory snapshot</strong> of the suspect VM (useful to capture running processes and keys in memory).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6566" data-end="6686">
<p data-start="6568" data-end="6686"><strong data-start="6568" data-end="6582">Disk image</strong> (or container image) — preserve <code data-start="6615" data-end="6626">/var/log/</code>, <code data-start="6628" data-end="6636">/home/</code>, active conda/venv envs, <code data-start="6662" data-end="6669">/opt/</code> installations.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6687" data-end="6775">
<p data-start="6689" data-end="6775"><strong data-start="6689" data-end="6718">List of running processes</strong> and their cmdlines (including container runtime info).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6776" data-end="6868">
<p data-start="6778" data-end="6868"><strong data-start="6778" data-end="6798">GPU process list</strong> (what process is bound to <code data-start="6825" data-end="6833">nvidia</code> devices) and unloaded libraries.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6869" data-end="6960">
<p data-start="6871" data-end="6960"><strong data-start="6871" data-end="6902">Container runtimes &amp; images</strong>: <code data-start="6904" data-end="6919">docker images</code>, <code data-start="6921" data-end="6936">podman images</code>, K8s pod definitions.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6961" data-end="7026">
<p data-start="6963" data-end="7026"><strong data-start="6963" data-end="6990">Pip/conda package lists</strong> and any <code data-start="6999" data-end="7017">requirements.txt</code> files.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7027" data-end="7121">
<p data-start="7029" data-end="7121"><strong data-start="7029" data-end="7054">Network flow captures</strong> for the timeframe (to see where checkpoints/data were uploaded).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7122" data-end="7264">
<p data-start="7124" data-end="7264"><strong data-start="7124" data-end="7147">Any model artifacts</strong> found (.pt, checkpoint directories). Hash and preserve them — they can be used to attribute to known leaks or forks.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="7266" data-end="7269">
<h2 data-start="7271" data-end="7326">5) Response &amp; remediation playbook (short checklist)</h2>
<ol data-start="7328" data-end="8366">
<li data-start="7328" data-end="7422">
<p data-start="7331" data-end="7422"><strong data-start="7331" data-end="7342">Isolate</strong>: Take the instance or node offline (or detach from network) if safe to do so.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7423" data-end="7504">
<p data-start="7426" data-end="7504"><strong data-start="7426" data-end="7447">Preserve evidence</strong>: snapshot disk and memory, collect logs before reboot.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7505" data-end="7611">
<p data-start="7508" data-end="7611"><strong data-start="7508" data-end="7530">Rotate credentials</strong>: immediately revoke and rotate any compromised API keys or service principals.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7612" data-end="7732">
<p data-start="7615" data-end="7732"><strong data-start="7615" data-end="7631">Block egress</strong>: block suspected outbound endpoints (S3 buckets, known C2) via firewall or cloud network controls.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7733" data-end="7843">
<p data-start="7736" data-end="7843"><strong data-start="7736" data-end="7767">Search for lateral movement</strong>: hunt for other instances spun up by the same identity or similar timing.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7844" data-end="7971">
<p data-start="7847" data-end="7971"><strong data-start="7847" data-end="7866">Engage provider</strong>: use cloud vendor abuse/takedown channels; get assistance with their internal logs and IP attribution.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7972" data-end="8090">
<p data-start="7975" data-end="8090"><strong data-start="7975" data-end="7996">Forensic analysis</strong>: examine model artifacts, installed packages, user accounts, and cron jobs for persistence.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="8091" data-end="8236">
<p data-start="8094" data-end="8236"><strong data-start="8094" data-end="8116">Legal &amp; regulatory</strong>: preserve chain of custody for law enforcement coordination; capture billing/payment evidence if extortion suspected.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="8237" data-end="8366">
<p data-start="8240" data-end="8366"><strong data-start="8240" data-end="8253">Remediate</strong>: reprovision clean instances, apply patches, enforce hardened AMIs/Images, and improve account security posture.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="8368" data-end="8371">
<h2 data-start="8373" data-end="8446">6) Prevention controls — policy &amp; engineering (prioritized, easy wins)</h2>
<p data-start="8448" data-end="8484"><strong data-start="8448" data-end="8484">Quick wins (immediate, high ROI)</strong></p>
<ul data-start="8485" data-end="9055">
<li data-start="8485" data-end="8584">
<p data-start="8487" data-end="8584">Enforce <strong data-start="8495" data-end="8513">billing alerts</strong> for GPU/accelerator families and set thresholds per account/project.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="8585" data-end="8692">
<p data-start="8587" data-end="8692"><strong data-start="8587" data-end="8603">Require tags</strong> for any GPU instance (owner, purpose, ticket ID) and auto-block untagged provisioning.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="8693" data-end="8865">
<p data-start="8695" data-end="8865">Apply <strong data-start="8701" data-end="8718">IAM hardening</strong>: MFA for cloud console, restrict <code data-start="8752" data-end="8768">iam:CreateUser</code>/<code data-start="8769" data-end="8785">iam:CreateRole</code>, require approvals for creating service principals that can create instances.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="8866" data-end="8955">
<p data-start="8868" data-end="8955">Centralize cloud accounts: <strong data-start="8895" data-end="8920">no unmanaged accounts</strong> that can spawn GPUs anonymously.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="8956" data-end="9055">
<p data-start="8958" data-end="9055">Block public S3 buckets and require server-side encryption for buckets used by compute workloads.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="9057" data-end="9072"><strong data-start="9057" data-end="9072">Medium term</strong></p>
<ul data-start="9073" data-end="9435">
<li data-start="9073" data-end="9178">
<p data-start="9075" data-end="9178"><strong data-start="9075" data-end="9105">Whitelist container images</strong> allowed to run with GPU access in Kubernetes; scan images for ML libs.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="9179" data-end="9264">
<p data-start="9181" data-end="9264">Implement <strong data-start="9191" data-end="9211">GPU quota limits</strong> per team and require approval for quota increases.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="9265" data-end="9359">
<p data-start="9267" data-end="9359">Deploy <strong data-start="9274" data-end="9295">runtime detection</strong> (Falco, Sysmon, EDR agents) to flag ML-like process activity.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="9360" data-end="9435">
<p data-start="9362" data-end="9435">Integrate cloud provider abuse feeds into SIEM for near-real time alerts.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="9437" data-end="9450"><strong data-start="9437" data-end="9450">Strategic</strong></p>
<ul data-start="9451" data-end="9754">
<li data-start="9451" data-end="9568">
<p data-start="9453" data-end="9568">Enforce <strong data-start="9461" data-end="9485">compute transparency</strong> in procurement: log orders/allocations for on-prem and colocation GPU purchases.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="9569" data-end="9661">
<p data-start="9571" data-end="9661">Work with legal/compliance to require <strong data-start="9609" data-end="9643">KYC for high-FLOP cloud orders</strong> where possible.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="9662" data-end="9754">
<p data-start="9664" data-end="9754">Participate in sector <strong data-start="9686" data-end="9713">abuse-sharing consortia</strong> (share telemetry on GPU abuse patterns).</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="9756" data-end="9759">
<h2 data-start="9761" data-end="9816">7) Indicators of Compromise / Prioritization scoring</h2>
<p data-start="9817" data-end="9913">When triaging, score events where multiple signals co-occur. Examples of high-risk combinations:</p>
<ul data-start="9915" data-end="10221">
<li data-start="9915" data-end="10023">
<p data-start="9917" data-end="10023"><code data-start="9917" data-end="9939">GPU instance created</code> + <code data-start="9942" data-end="9975">large upload to external bucket</code> + <code data-start="9978" data-end="10001">new service principal</code> = <strong data-start="10004" data-end="10021">High priority</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="10024" data-end="10120">
<p data-start="10026" data-end="10120"><code data-start="10026" data-end="10058">Sustained high GPU utilization</code> + <code data-start="10061" data-end="10098">presence of model files (.pt/.ckpt)</code> = <strong data-start="10101" data-end="10118">High priority</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="10121" data-end="10221">
<p data-start="10123" data-end="10221"><code data-start="10123" data-end="10175">GPU instance created by known internal DevOps user</code> + <code data-start="10178" data-end="10192">tagged as ML</code> = <strong data-start="10195" data-end="10219">Low priority / valid</strong></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="10223" data-end="10274">Use such composite rules to reduce false positives.</p>
<hr data-start="10276" data-end="10279">
<h2 data-start="10281" data-end="10328">8) Quick example hunts you can implement now</h2>
<p data-start="10329" data-end="10378">(Translate to your tooling; these are conceptual)</p>
<ul data-start="10380" data-end="10817">
<li data-start="10380" data-end="10489">
<p data-start="10382" data-end="10489">Alert: <code data-start="10389" data-end="10487">count(created_instances where instance_type in GPU_FAMILIES and creator not in ML_ALLOWLIST) &gt; 0</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="10490" data-end="10550">
<p data-start="10492" data-end="10550">Alert: <code data-start="10499" data-end="10548">sum(gpu_hours) by account over 24h &gt; baseline*4</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="10551" data-end="10632">
<p data-start="10553" data-end="10632">Hunt: <code data-start="10559" data-end="10630">find files matching *.pt OR *checkpoint* on non-ML buckets and assets</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="10633" data-end="10754">
<p data-start="10635" data-end="10754">Hunt: <code data-start="10641" data-end="10735">processes with cmdline contains ("torch","tensorflow","trainer","accelerate","bitsandbytes")</code> on non-ML assets</p>
</li>
<li data-start="10755" data-end="10817">
<p data-start="10757" data-end="10817">Network: <code data-start="10766" data-end="10815">alert on S3 PutObject &gt; 1GB from compute subnet</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="10819" data-end="10822">
<h2 data-start="10824" data-end="10856">9) Collaboration &amp; escalation</h2>
<ul data-start="10857" data-end="11280">
<li data-start="10857" data-end="10966">
<p data-start="10859" data-end="10966"><strong data-start="10859" data-end="10878">Cloud providers</strong>: use their abuse/contact channels and request their internal logs when investigating.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="10967" data-end="11072">
<p data-start="10969" data-end="11072"><strong data-start="10969" data-end="10997">Exchanges / AML partners</strong>: if you see ransomware payments, coordinate with exchanges for KYC info.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="11073" data-end="11174">
<p data-start="11075" data-end="11174"><strong data-start="11075" data-end="11091">Peer sharing</strong>: share IOCs with sector peers and CERTs (don't publish sensitive IoCs publicly).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="11175" data-end="11280">
<p data-start="11177" data-end="11280"><strong data-start="11177" data-end="11196">Law enforcement</strong>: prepare preserved evidence and timeline for MLATs if cross-border action required.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="11282" data-end="11285">
<h2 data-start="11287" data-end="11336">10) Summary — what CISOs should do immediately</h2>
<ol data-start="11337" data-end="11713">
<li data-start="11337" data-end="11411">
<p data-start="11340" data-end="11411">Turn on <strong data-start="11348" data-end="11380">billing and GPU-quota alerts</strong> (cover every cloud account).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="11412" data-end="11488">
<p data-start="11415" data-end="11488">Enforce <strong data-start="11423" data-end="11445">tagging &amp; approval</strong> for any instance that can request a GPU.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="11489" data-end="11566">
<p data-start="11492" data-end="11566">Add <strong data-start="11496" data-end="11515">runtime EDR/NDR</strong> + container image whitelisting for GPU clusters.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="11567" data-end="11638">
<p data-start="11570" data-end="11638">Hunt for <code data-start="11579" data-end="11584">.pt</code>/checkpoint files and large uploads in past 90 days.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="11639" data-end="11713">
<p data-start="11642" data-end="11713">Build a GPU-forensics checklist with legal and provider contact points.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="11715" data-end="11718">
<p data-start="11720" data-end="11741">If you’d like, I can:</p>
<ul data-start="11742" data-end="12036">
<li data-start="11742" data-end="11849">
<p data-start="11744" data-end="11849">produce <strong data-start="11752" data-end="11784">concrete SIEM query examples</strong> in Splunk / Elastic / SumoLogic syntax tailored to your stack,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="11850" data-end="11931">
<p data-start="11852" data-end="11931">draft a <strong data-start="11860" data-end="11887">GPU-forensics checklist</strong> (one-page) you can hand to DFIR teams, or</p>
</li>
<li data-start="11932" data-end="12036">
<p data-start="11934" data-end="12036">create an <strong data-start="11944" data-end="11964">alerting ruleset</strong> (YAML) for Kubernetes admission controllers to block untagged GPU pods.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="12038" data-end="12078">Which of those would be most useful now?</p>

class="whitespace-pre! language-markdown"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># 🧠 Detecting and Preventing GPU Abuse in Cloud Environments</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Audience:**</span></span><span> CISOs, SOC teams, DFIR analysts, cloud security engineers, and law enforcement cyber units.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Purpose:**</span></span><span> Provide a defensive framework for detecting and mitigating illicit GPU usage for unauthorized AI model training or “GPU botnet” activity.  

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 1️⃣ Threat Model — What GPU Abuse Looks Like</span></span><span>

Attackers increasingly attempt to hijack GPU resources (either cloud or on-prem) for high-compute tasks such as:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Unauthorized </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**LLM training or fine-tuning**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Crypto mining**</span></span><span> disguised as ML workloads
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Data exfiltration**</span></span><span> using ML frameworks
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Malware hosting**</span></span><span> within containerized GPU jobs

Typical vectors:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Compromised API keys or IAM roles  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Misconfigured Kubernetes clusters with exposed GPU nodes  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Stolen cloud credentials used to spin up GPU instances  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Compromised developer workstations repurposed for distributed ML workloads  

This README provides </span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">*detection and response*</span></span><span> guidance only — </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**no offensive or exploit detail.**</span></span><span>

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 2️⃣ Best Detectors — Cloud, Host, and Network Telemetry</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### ☁️ Cloud Provider / Billing Signals</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Billing spikes**</span></span><span> for GPU instance families (A100, H100, MI300).  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Instance creation anomalies**</span></span><span> — GPUs spun up in new regions or by non-ML accounts.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Ephemeral credential usage**</span></span><span> with high-value IAM actions.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Interactive console sessions**</span></span><span> in accounts not normally accessed manually.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Correlated API calls:**</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`RunInstances`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`CreateInstance`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`CreateRole`</span></span><span> outside maintenance windows.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 💻 Host / Container Indicators</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Sustained </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU utilization &gt;70%**</span></span><span> for &gt;30 minutes on non-ML hosts.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Long-running Python processes**</span></span><span> invoking ML frameworks (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`torch`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`tensorflow`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`transformers`</span></span><span>).  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Files or folders named </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`checkpoints/`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.pt`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.bin`</span></span><span>, or </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.ckpt`</span></span><span>.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Unexpected </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**ML container images**</span></span><span> (e.g., </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`pytorch`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`huggingface/transformers`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`tensorflow`</span></span><span>).  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Environment variables**</span></span><span> exposing GPUs (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`</span></span><span>).  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Kubernetes pods requesting </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`nvidia.com/gpu`</span></span><span> resources in namespaces not tagged for ML.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 🌐 Network / Storage</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Multi-GB uploads to external storage (S3, Azure Blob, GCS).  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Data transfers to </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**HuggingFace**</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**private Git hosts**</span></span><span>, or </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**unknown storage endpoints**</span></span><span>.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Creation of new storage buckets followed by heavy outbound transfers.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Traffic to model sharing domains or cloud buckets not listed in allow-lists.  

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 3️⃣ SOC Hunt Ideas (Non-Actionable Examples)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; These examples describe <span class="hljs-strong">**detection concepts**</span></span></span><span> only; translate to Splunk, Elastic, or your SIEM syntax.

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Cloud audit log hunt:**</span></span><span> find </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`CreateInstance`</span></span><span> / </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`RunInstances`</span></span><span> events for GPU instance types by users outside ML teams.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Billing anomaly:**</span></span><span> alert if GPU spend &gt; 3× baseline in any 24-hour period.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Image detection:**</span></span><span> flag Docker/K8s images containing ML frameworks where none are expected.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**File artifact search:**</span></span><span> hunt for </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.pt`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.bin`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.ckpt`</span></span><span> files on non-ML servers.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Process behavior:**</span></span><span> detect </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`python`</span></span><span> processes with both network activity and sustained GPU load.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Egress watch:**</span></span><span> alert when uploads &gt;1 GB occur from GPU instances to external endpoints.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU metric anomalies:**</span></span><span> sustained high GPU temperature or power draw outside scheduled workloads.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 4️⃣ Forensics &amp; Evidence Preservation</span></span><span>

If GPU abuse is suspected:

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">1.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Snapshot cloud resources:**</span></span><span> capture VM, container, and disk states.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">2.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Preserve audit logs:**</span></span><span> CloudTrail, Audit Logs, Kubernetes API logs.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">3.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Memory snapshot:**</span></span><span> capture running process space if allowed.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">4.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Collect filesystem artifacts:**</span></span><span>  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">   -</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`/var/log/`</span></span><span> and </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`/home/`</span></span><span>  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">   -</span></span><span> ML artifacts (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`*.pt`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`trainer_state.json`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`opt_state.pt`</span></span><span>)  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">   -</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`requirements.txt`</span></span><span>, environment files  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">5.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**List GPU-bound processes:**</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`nvidia-smi`</span></span><span> or equivalent; note PID mappings.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">6.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Network flow capture:**</span></span><span> outbound endpoints, storage URLs, IPs.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">7.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Container evidence:**</span></span><span> list running images, hashes, and registries used.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">8.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Hash model artifacts**</span></span><span> for later correlation with known leaks.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">9.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Preserve chain of custody**</span></span><span> if law enforcement involvement is expected.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 5️⃣ Response Checklist</span></span><span>

| Step | Action | Goal |
|------|--------|------|
| 1 | </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Isolate**</span></span><span> suspect nodes | Prevent further misuse |
| 2 | </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Preserve**</span></span><span> evidence before reboot | For forensics |
| 3 | </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Revoke/rotate**</span></span><span> credentials | Stop recurring access |
| 4 | </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Block egress**</span></span><span> to malicious endpoints | Contain data exfil |
| 5 | </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Search for lateral movement**</span></span><span> | Identify additional compromised accounts |
| 6 | </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Engage cloud provider**</span></span><span> abuse channels | Obtain deeper logs |
| 7 | </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Perform forensic review**</span></span><span> of artifacts | Attribute activity |
| 8 | </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Rebuild / patch**</span></span><span> compromised systems | Restore clean state |
| 9 | </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Coordinate**</span></span><span> with law enforcement &amp; CERTs | Legal and joint mitigation |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 6️⃣ Prevention Controls</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 🔧 Quick Wins</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Enable billing alerts**</span></span><span> for GPU families and quota increases.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Require instance tagging**</span></span><span> (owner, purpose) for all GPU provisioning.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**MFA and just-in-time access**</span></span><span> for IAM and console logins.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Auto-block untagged GPU instances.**</span></span><span>  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Restrict public S3 buckets**</span></span><span> and enable encryption by default.  

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### ⚙️ Medium-Term</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Whitelisted container images**</span></span><span> with GPU access only for approved registries.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU quota limits**</span></span><span> per team with ticketed approvals.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Runtime detection**</span></span><span> via EDR / Falco / Sysmon.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Automated anomaly detection**</span></span><span> on GPU metrics and egress volume.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 🧱 Strategic</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Centralize compute procurement**</span></span><span> with identity tracking.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Monitor GPU orders and hardware inventory.**</span></span><span>  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Collaborate with providers**</span></span><span> on compute-abuse intelligence feeds.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Implement compute transparency**</span></span><span> reporting for regulators.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 7️⃣ Indicators of Compromise (IOC) Correlation</span></span><span>

| Indicator | Description | Risk |
|------------|--------------|------|
| GPU instance + large data upload | Sudden training or exfil attempt | 🔴 High |
| GPU process + model files detected | Unauthorized model training | 🔴 High |
| Tagged ML workload, valid owner | Legitimate usage | 🟢 Low |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 8️⃣ Detection Rules You Can Deploy Now</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Cloud rule:**</span></span><span> alert if </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`instanceType ∈ GPU_FAMILY`</span></span><span> and creator ∉ ML allowlist.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Billing rule:**</span></span><span> alert if </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`gpu_hours`</span></span><span> &gt; baseline × 4.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**File rule:**</span></span><span> scan for </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.pt`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.ckpt`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`checkpoint/`</span></span><span> directories.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Process rule:**</span></span><span> alert on </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`python`</span></span><span> using </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`torch`</span></span><span> or </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`tensorflow`</span></span><span> on non-ML hosts.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Network rule:**</span></span><span> alert on outbound upload &gt; 1 GB to non-approved endpoints.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 9️⃣ Collaboration &amp; Escalation</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Cloud Providers:**</span></span><span> contact abuse or incident-response teams for deeper telemetry.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Exchanges / AML Partners:**</span></span><span> trace ransomware or laundering attempts tied to cloud spend.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Peer Organizations:**</span></span><span> share indicators via ISAC / CERT networks.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Law Enforcement:**</span></span><span> provide preserved logs, hashes, and wallet traces.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🔟 Executive Summary for CISOs</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">1.</span></span><span> Turn on </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU quota and billing alerts**</span></span><span> for all accounts.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">2.</span></span><span> Require </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**instance tagging**</span></span><span> for GPU provisioning.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">3.</span></span><span> Deploy </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**runtime GPU utilization monitoring**</span></span><span> (EDR + cloud metrics).  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">4.</span></span><span> Regularly </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**hunt for model artifacts**</span></span><span> (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.pt`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.ckpt`</span></span><span>) across storage.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">5.</span></span><span> Maintain a </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU Forensics &amp; Escalation Plan**</span></span><span> shared with legal and DFIR teams.  

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### ⚖️ Disclaimer</span></span><span>
This document is for </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**defensive and educational use only**</span></span><span>. It contains no exploit or offensive procedures.  
All examples are intended for lawful security operations and incident-response planning.

---

class="whitespace-pre! language-markdown"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># 🔍 GPU Forensics &amp; Incident Response Checklist</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Purpose:**</span></span><span>  
Provide a structured, defensible checklist for investigating suspected GPU misuse — including unauthorized AI model training, cryptomining, or data exfiltration via GPU workloads.  
Designed for DFIR, SOC, and law enforcement teams operating in cloud or hybrid environments.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🧠 1. Pre-Investigation Preparation</span></span><span>

| Task | Description | Responsible |
|------|--------------|--------------|
| 🔸 Confirm authorization | Ensure you have incident-response or legal approval to collect cloud evidence. | Legal / IR Lead |
| 🔸 Identify scope | Determine whether incident involves cloud, on-prem, or hybrid GPU infrastructure. | Incident Commander |
| 🔸 Assign roles | Define leads for cloud forensics, host forensics, network analysis, and evidence management. | IR Manager |
| 🔸 Preserve chain of custody | Document each evidence collection step. Use immutable storage for artifacts. | All Teams |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## ☁️ 2. Cloud Evidence Collection</span></span><span>

| Artifact | Description / Command | Notes |
|-----------|----------------------|-------|
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Audit Logs**</span></span><span> | AWS CloudTrail, Azure Activity Logs, GCP Audit — filter for </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`RunInstances`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`CreateInstance`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`CreateRole`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`StartVM`</span></span><span> events. | Establish provisioning timeline. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Billing Records**</span></span><span> | Capture billing &amp; GPU-hour data for the time window. | Identify anomalies / misuse cost. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Instance Metadata**</span></span><span> | Collect instance details: type, region, tags, image ID, user data. | Confirms GPU family (A100/H100/etc). |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**IAM Activity**</span></span><span> | Download recent IAM changes, token creation events, MFA usage. | Tracks compromised creds. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Snapshots**</span></span><span> | Create disk snapshots or machine images for forensic duplication. | Verify before shutdown. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Network Flow Logs**</span></span><span> | Export VPC Flow Logs or equivalent. | Detect exfil endpoints. |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 💻 3. Host &amp; Container Forensics</span></span><span>

| Artifact | Command / Collection Method | Purpose |
|-----------|----------------------------|----------|
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Process Listing**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`ps aux`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`top`</span></span><span>, or </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`nvidia-smi -l 1`</span></span><span> | Identify long-running GPU-bound processes. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Running Containers**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`docker ps -a`</span></span><span> / </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`kubectl get pods -A`</span></span><span> | Detect ML framework containers. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Container Images**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`docker images`</span></span><span> / </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`ctr images ls`</span></span><span> | Hash and store image metadata. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Python Environments**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`pip freeze`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`conda list`</span></span><span> | Detect </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`torch`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`tensorflow`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`transformers`</span></span><span> installs. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**ML Artifacts**</span></span><span> | Search for </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.pt`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.bin`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.ckpt`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`trainer_state.json`</span></span><span>. | Proves model training occurred. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**User Accounts &amp; SSH Keys**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`/etc/passwd`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`~/.ssh/authorized_keys`</span></span><span> | Identify unauthorized users. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Cron / Scheduled Jobs**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`crontab -l`</span></span><span> / </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`/etc/cron*`</span></span><span> | Detect persistence or auto-start tasks. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Logs**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`/var/log/auth.log`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`/var/log/syslog`</span></span><span>, container logs. | Identify timeline and commands used. |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🧩 4. GPU Hardware &amp; Utilization Artifacts</span></span><span>

| Artifact | Command / Tool | Insight |
|-----------|----------------|---------|
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU process mapping**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`nvidia-smi pmon -c 1`</span></span><span> | Which PID is consuming GPU cycles. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU memory snapshot**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY`</span></span><span> | Confirms VRAM use / workload intensity. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Driver &amp; firmware info**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`nvidia-smi -q -d DRIVER,FAN,POWER`</span></span><span> | Confirms driver integrity and versions. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU kernel logs**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`dmesg | grep -i nvidia`</span></span><span> | Detects driver crashes or injections. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Performance metrics**</span></span><span> | Cloud metrics (CloudWatch, Stackdriver) | Long-term utilization graphs. |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🌐 5. Network &amp; Storage Investigation</span></span><span>

| Artifact | Description | Purpose |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Outbound endpoints**</span></span><span> | Correlate destination IPs with threat intel. | Detect data exfil or remote control. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Data uploads**</span></span><span> | Look for large (&gt;1 GB) uploads to unknown storage buckets. | Confirms exfil / model sync. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Bucket enumeration**</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`aws s3 ls`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`gsutil ls`</span></span><span>, etc. | Identify attacker-created storage. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**DNS / Proxy logs**</span></span><span> | Resolve domains tied to ML-sharing or malware sites. | Contextual attribution. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**PCAP / Flow captures**</span></span><span> | Collect short-term network traces. | Support timeline reconstruction. |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 📦 6. Evidence Preservation &amp; Integrity</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Use </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**forensic imaging tools**</span></span><span> (e.g., </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`dd`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`FTK Imager`</span></span><span>, cloud snapshot APIs).  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Compute </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**SHA256 hashes**</span></span><span> of all collected files and images.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Store artifacts in </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**immutable evidence storage**</span></span><span> (e.g., WORM S3 buckets).  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Maintain </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**evidence log**</span></span><span> with timestamp, collector name, and tool used.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Create a </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**case summary**</span></span><span> including: instance IDs, IPs, IAM users, and observed behaviors.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## ⚙️ 7. Analysis Phase</span></span><span>

| Step | Analysis Goal |
|------|----------------|
| 1 | Reconstruct timeline of GPU provisioning → workload execution → teardown. |
| 2 | Correlate IAM logs with API actions (who created what). |
| 3 | Identify model files or datasets (possible intellectual property theft). |
| 4 | Attribute activity to known malware / threat actor if signatures exist. |
| 5 | Quantify compute hours used and potential cost impact. |
| 6 | Determine persistence mechanisms (if any). |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🛡️ 8. Remediation</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">1.</span></span><span> Rotate all </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**IAM/API credentials**</span></span><span> associated with the incident.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">2.</span></span><span> Delete or quarantine compromised GPU instances.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">3.</span></span><span> Patch or reimage affected workloads.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">4.</span></span><span> Enable </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU quota and billing alerts**</span></span><span> moving forward.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">5.</span></span><span> Apply stronger </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**KYC &amp; tagging**</span></span><span> for GPU resources.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">6.</span></span><span> Audit network egress controls and restrict external uploads.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">7.</span></span><span> Coordinate with </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**cloud provider abuse teams**</span></span><span> for account review.  

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🧾 9. Reporting &amp; Disclosure</span></span><span>

| Output | Audience | Content |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Internal IR Report**</span></span><span> | Executive / CISO | Summary, timeline, impact, next steps |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Provider Incident Ticket**</span></span><span> | Cloud vendor | Instance IDs, logs, artifacts |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Regulatory / Legal Notice**</span></span><span> | Legal / Compliance | Data exposure, PII indicators |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Law Enforcement Packet**</span></span><span> | CERT / FBI / Europol | Evidence log, forensic hashes, wallet traces |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🧭 10. Post-Incident Hardening</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Enforce </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**GPU tagging and ownership policy.**</span></span><span>  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Review </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**IAM least-privilege**</span></span><span> and enforce MFA.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Implement </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**real-time GPU utilization alerts.**</span></span><span>  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Deploy </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**runtime EDR or anomaly detection**</span></span><span> on GPU workloads.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Document lessons learned and feed into continuous monitoring.  

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### ⚖️ Disclaimer</span></span><span>
This checklist is for </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**defensive, forensic, and educational use only**</span></span><span>.  
It contains no exploit code or offensive procedures.  
All steps must be performed under legal authority and corporate incident-response policy.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">_Last updated: November 7 2025_</span></span><span>  
</span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">*Prepared collaboratively with ChatGPT (OpenAI, model GPT-5) for the `dark-llm-mitigations` repository.*</span></span><span>

class="whitespace-pre! language-markdown"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># ⚙️ GPU Abuse &amp; Covert AI Training Detection — iSIEM Query Guide</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Audience:**</span></span><span> SOC analysts, detection engineers, and incident responders.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Purpose:**</span></span><span> Provide contextual SIEM queries and analytic logic for detecting illicit GPU usage, unauthorized LLM training, or compute abuse in cloud and hybrid environments.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Scope:**</span></span><span> Defensive only — all queries focus on detection and alerting, not offensive or exploitative actions.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🧩 1. Detection Philosophy</span></span><span>

GPU misuse for illicit AI workloads leaves </span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">*correlated traces*</span></span><span> across:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Cloud audit logs (instance creation, quota changes)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Host telemetry (processes, GPU metrics)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Network flows (large data transfers, unknown endpoints)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Storage access logs (large uploads, new buckets)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Billing/usage anomalies (spending spikes)

The following queries are intended for:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Proactive hunting**</span></span><span>  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Real-time alerting**</span></span><span>  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Anomaly detection baselining**</span></span><span>

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## ☁️ 2. Cloud Audit Log Queries</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Splunk — AWS CloudTrail / Azure Activity / GCP Audit Logs</span></span><span>

<span class="hljs-code">```spl
index=cloud_audit_logs
(eventName="RunInstances" OR eventName="CreateInstance" OR eventName="Compute.Instances.insert")
| eval instanceType=coalesce(requestParameters.instanceType, json_extract(request, "$.protoPayload.request.machineType"))
| search instanceType IN ("p4d*", "p5*", "a100*", "h100*", "mi300*", "v100*")
| stats count BY userIdentity.arn, instanceType, sourceIPAddress, region
| where count &gt; 0
</span></span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="1768" data-end="1977"><strong data-start="1768" data-end="1780">Context:</strong><br data-start="1780" data-end="1783">
Flags new GPU instance provisioning. Filter by instance family names (A100, H100, MI300, V100, etc.).<br data-start="1884" data-end="1887">
Use for baseline deviation — any creation event from a non-ML user identity is suspicious.</p>

  </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">AND</span></span><span> gpu_utilization </span><span><span class="hljs-operator">&gt;</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-number">70</span></span><span>
  </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">AND</span></span><span> duration_seconds </span><span><span class="hljs-operator">&gt;</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-number">600</span></span><span>;

<p data-start="3044" data-end="3208"><strong data-start="3044" data-end="3056">Context:</strong><br data-start="3056" data-end="3059">
Flags long-running Python processes with GPU load &gt;70% for &gt;10 min.<br data-start="3126" data-end="3129">
Excellent for identifying unauthorized LLM training, mining, or inference jobs.</p>

Useful for identifying model checkpoints or data dumps.</p>

<p data-start="6023" data-end="6160"><strong data-start="6023" data-end="6035">Context:</strong><br data-start="6035" data-end="6038">
Correlates instance creation → GPU training → large upload within 1 hour.<br data-start="6111" data-end="6114">
Strong indicator of unauthorized LLM activity.</p>
<hr data-start="6162" data-end="6165">
<h2 data-start="6167" data-end="6205">🔍 8. Anomaly-Based Detection Ideas</h2>
<ul data-start="6207" data-end="6642">
<li data-start="6207" data-end="6318">
<p data-start="6209" data-end="6318"><strong data-start="6209" data-end="6237">GPU-hours anomaly model:</strong><br data-start="6237" data-end="6240">
Train a baseline of <code data-start="6262" data-end="6273">gpu_hours</code> per user/project → alert on 3σ deviations.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6319" data-end="6430">
<p data-start="6321" data-end="6430"><strong data-start="6321" data-end="6354">Cluster-level GPU contention:</strong><br data-start="6354" data-end="6357">
Detect sudden drops in available GPU quota (from Kubernetes metrics).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6431" data-end="6548">
<p data-start="6433" data-end="6548"><strong data-start="6433" data-end="6461">Process lineage anomaly:</strong><br data-start="6461" data-end="6464">
Flag new Python processes spawned by non-interactive shells or service accounts.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6549" data-end="6642">
<p data-start="6551" data-end="6642"><strong data-start="6551" data-end="6572">Dataflow anomaly:</strong><br data-start="6572" data-end="6575">
Alert on first-seen destination domain from GPU cluster subnet.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="6644" data-end="6647">
<h2 data-start="6649" data-end="6677">🧾 9. Output &amp; Escalation</h2>
<ul data-start="6679" data-end="6995">
<li data-start="6679" data-end="6749">
<p data-start="6681" data-end="6749">Send confirmed hits to <strong data-start="6704" data-end="6722">Tier-3 or DFIR</strong> for artifact collection.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6750" data-end="6811">
<p data-start="6752" data-end="6811">Cross-reference with <strong data-start="6773" data-end="6789">billing data</strong> for compute impact.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6812" data-end="6903">
<p data-start="6814" data-end="6903">Generate <strong data-start="6823" data-end="6848">cloud support tickets</strong> if confirmed abuse involves provider infrastructure.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6904" data-end="6995">
<p data-start="6906" data-end="6995">For critical detections, notify <strong data-start="6938" data-end="6965">law enforcement or CERT</strong> if criminal misuse suspected.</p>
</li>
</ul>
